key.name: kinetic-scrolling
key.description:
Controls gtk_scrolled_window_set_kinetic_scrolling on the document scrolled window. When true (default), trackpad flicks coast and diagonal trackpad gestures pan in both axes simultaneously — the standard GTK behavior. When false, scroll events apply only the user-induced delta with no momentum, and diagonal motion is delivered to GTK as paired axis events.
The earlier default-false rationale (cap input to keep the render cache from outrunning) is obsolete since v0.14 introduced GThreadPool sort-function priority dispatch and v0.17 added fz_cookie mid-render abort: the cache responds to scroll velocity without needing an input-side cap.

key.name: reading-ruler
key.description: When true, dim the page everywhere except a horizontal band that tracks the mouse cursor. Useful for dense technical reading where keeping your eye on the active line is the failure mode. Toggleable from the primary menu; the setting persists across sessions.

key.name: loupe
key.summary: Show a magnifying loupe at the cursor
key.description: When true, render a circular zoomed view of the underlying page content centered on the mouse cursor. Useful for dense comic panels, small chart axis labels, and footnote text on scanned documents. The magnification factor is fixed at 2.5×. Toggleable from the primary menu or via F7; the setting persists.

key.name: crop-margins
key.summary: Auto-crop whitespace margins from PDF pages
key.description: When true, scan the current visible page's text via the cached structured-text page, compute the content bounding box, and apply the resulting margin fractions uniformly across the document. Pages render without their whitespace margins so the text occupies more of the screen — useful on small laptop screens with dense technical PDFs. Has no effect on backends that don't support stext-based content detection (DjVu, CBR). Toggleable from the primary menu or via F6; the setting persists.

key.name: manga-mode
key.description: When true, swap the directional page-navigation keys: Right Arrow moves to the previous page and Left Arrow moves to the next page, following the reading order of Japanese manga and Hebrew/Arabic documents. Combined with facing-pages mode, also flips the left/right layout within a pair so the right-hand page is the odd-numbered one. Toggleable from the primary menu or via F4.

key.name: webtoon-mode
key.summary: Seamless vertical strip layout (webtoon reading mode)
key.description: When true, drop the inter-page gap to zero so vertically-laid-out comics stitch into a single seamless strip. Designed for Korean webtoons and other long-strip formats where the artist composes across page boundaries. Has no visual effect when facing-pages is also active. Toggleable from the primary menu or via F5.

key.name: facing-pages
key.summary: Lay out pages side-by-side in pairs
key.description: When true, render two pages per row (page 0 paired with 1, 2 with 3, etc.) with a small gutter between them. Useful for comics with artwork that spans facing pages and for two-up reading of novels. With manga-mode also active, the pair order flips so the odd-numbered page sits on the left and the even-numbered page on the right. Toggleable from the primary menu or via F10.

key.name: reading-font-family
key.summary: Font family used for the body text of reflow documents
key.description: Pango font family name for paragraph text in EPUB / FB2 / TXT / MOBI / AZW3 reading. Empty string (the default) lets the system serif fallback take over. Set to "OpenDyslexic" or another locally-installed family to override. Picked from the Reading Settings dialog in the primary menu.

key.name: reading-font-size
key.summary: Font size in points for body text in reflow documents
key.description: Body-text font size, in points, applied to PARAGRAPH / BLOCKQUOTE / LIST_ITEM blocks in reflow documents. Headings scale relative to this value. Default of 13pt matches a comfortable laptop reading distance.

key.name: reading-line-height
key.summary: Line-height multiplier for body text in reflow documents

key.name: reading-monospace-family
key.summary: Monospace font family used for code blocks in reflow
key.description: Pango font family for CODE blocks and inline monospace spans in reflow documents. Empty string falls back to the system monospace alias. Set to a locally-installed monospace family (Iosevka, JetBrains Mono, etc.) to override.

key.name: reading-theme
key.summary: Color theme for EPUB reading (WebKit reflow path)
key.description: Reading theme for EPUB documents rendered through WebKitGTK. 'system' follows the desktop light/dark preference (read from the settings portal); 'light' is dark text on near-white; 'sepia' is warm paper; 'dark' is a Kanagawa Dragon-flavored dark. Sets CSS background / foreground / link colors; applied live without reopening the document.

key.name: publisher-styles
key.summary: Honour publisher stylesheets in reflow documents
key.description: When true (the default), EPUB documents render with the book's own stylesheets and embedded fonts, served through the internal resource scheme. The reading theme, chosen typography, and the reading column still take precedence over book-level styling. When false, publisher stylesheets are disabled live (no reload) and only the built-in reading stylesheet applies.

key.name: reading-two-column
key.summary: Render reflow documents as two columns side-by-side
key.description: When true, FwReflowView lays out two adjacent pages as a spread, splitting the viewport horizontally. Pagination recomputes at half-content-width so each column gets appropriate line wrapping. Page navigation advances by two pages per step. Toggleable from the Reading Settings dialog or via F10 while a reflow document is open.

key.name: prefer-fixed-layout
key.summary: Open ebooks as fixed pages instead of reflowed text
key.description: When true, reflow-eligible formats (EPUB / FB2 / MOBI / AZW3) are opened through the fixed-layout MuPDF backend rather than the native reflow pipeline. Useful for documents the reflow parser renders poorly. Toggling it re-opens the current document. No effect on PDF / DjVu / comics, which are always fixed-layout.
